title: Early rhythm control as a STRATEGY in atrial fibrillation: what the strategy trials report, and why their four registered primaries do not pool
question: In adults with atrial fibrillation, does an early rhythm-control STRATEGY -- antiarrhythmic drugs or ablation, chosen and escalated as a strategy rather than as a single procedure -- reduce cardiovascular death, stroke or hospitalisation compared with usual care?
question_provenance: Written as a question about a STRATEGY, not a procedure. The sibling reviews ask what a catheter ablation does; this one asks what a policy of controlling rhythm early does, which is why its search term set is the strategy vocabulary and not the procedure vocabulary.

split_provenance.why_split: The parent asked three questions under one title. This is the third: the strategy question. See DECIDED-ablation-af-review-2026-08-19.md

outcomes.name: Each trial's own registered primary composite
outcomes.definition: Time to first occurrence of the trial's registered primary composite endpoint.
outcomes.definition_note: THE FOUR TRIALS REGISTER FOUR DIFFERENT COMPOSITES and the difference is at the component level, not in the wording. Recorded structurally in `component_mismatch` rather than only in prose, because a component difference stated in prose is exactly what a reader skims.

withholding_question.question: does each trial report, AT ANY RANK -- primary, secondary or other -- an outcome matching what the others report, before any decision about which pools are possible?
withholding_question.why_the_answer_is_decisive_rather_than_u: RAFT-AF REGISTERS NO SECONDARY OUTCOME AT ALL. There is nothing below its primary to harmonise on, so no estimand can be shared by all four trials -- not because nobody looked, but because one of the four has nothing there. This is the opposite outcome to sglt2-hf and apixaban prophylaxis, where asking the same question RECOVERED a pool from secondary rank. The question is worth asking precisely because its answer is not predictable.
withholding_question.why_this_check_is_a_check_and_not_a_bias: A CHECK WHOSE ANSWER IS NOT PREDICTABLE IS A CHECK; ONE THAT ALWAYS RECOVERS IS A BIAS. The same question was asked on three topics in one night and gave two different answers: on sglt2-hf and on apixaban prophylaxis it RECOVERED a pool from an estimand sitting at secondary rank, and here it returns a DECISIVE NO -- RAFT-AF registers no secondary outcome at all, so there is nothing below its primary to harmonise on. This review records the negative as evidence that the procedure is capable of returning one.

trials.name: EAST-AFNET 4

effect.derivation_note: The hazard ratio and its interval are stored as the source prints them, at the level the source prints them at. The log point and log standard error are DERIVED here, the standard error from the width of the printed interval using the multiplier belonging to that interval's own level -- 1.96 at 95 per cent and 2.054 at the 96 per cent EAST-AFNET 4 printed -- and neither is claimed to appear in any source.

source_quotes: A composite of cardiovascular death, stroke and hospitalization due to worsening of heart failure or due to acute coronary syndrome.

The 1st co-primary outcome parameter is defined as the time to the first occurrence of a composite of cardiovascular death, stroke / transient ischemic attack (TIA), and hospitalization due to worsening of heart failure or due to acute coronary syndrome.

A first-primary-outcome event occurred in 249 of the patients assigned to early rhythm control (3.9 per 100 person-years) and in 316 patients assigned to usual care (5.0 per 100 person-years) (hazard ratio, 0.79; 96% confidence interval, 0.66 to 0.94; P = 0.005)
provenance.quote_note: Three quotes: the endpoint TITLE as the registry states it, the registry's or the report's fuller DEFINITION of what those events are, and the RESULT sentence carrying the number stored. The first two say what was counted and the third says what happened, and this object exists partly because those were once confused.

primary.outcome_definition: A composite of cardiovascular death, stroke and hospitalization due to worsening of heart failure or due to acute coronary syndrome.
primary.registry_results_status: This trial's registry record posts NO results section.
primary.corrected_2026_08_17: THE ARMS WERE SWAPPED. The object labelled the 249-event arm 'Usual care' and gave it the role TREATMENT; the trial's own sentence assigns those 249 events to EARLY RHYTHM CONTROL. The label came from the registry's arm order and the count from the publication's, and the two differ. The derived odds ratio 0.7412 was unaffected in magnitude, which is why nothing caught it: the numbers were consistent and the labels were not. The interval was also computed at 95% where the trial printed 96%.

trials.design: randomised, open-label; early standardised RHYTHM CONTROL -- antiarrhythmic drugs or ablation -- against usual care
trials.comparator_type_basis: Every trial in this object randomises against an ACTIVE strategy -- medical therapy, drug therapy, usual care or rate control -- and none against placebo. Read from each registry record's arm types, where no arm is typed PLACEBO_COMPARATOR.
trials.subject_scope_flag: THIS TRIAL'S INTERVENTION IS NOT ABLATION. It is early standardised rhythm control against usual care -- a strategy arm in which most patients received antiarrhythmic drugs. It sits in a review about ablation, and that is recorded here rather than quietly resolved: a review whose title names a comparison its trials do not all make is the DOAC-versus-warfarin defect, and this object should be re-scoped or this trial removed by a human decision, not by this script.
trials.registration_brief_title: Early Treatment of Atrial Fibrillation for Stroke Prevention Trial
registered_primaries: A composite of cardiovascular death, stroke and hospitalization due to worsening of heart failure or due to acute coronary syndrome.
registered_secondaries: Key 2d outcomes: Each of the components of the 1st outcome, time to recurrent AF, cv hospitalizations, all-cause hospitalizations, left ventricular function, QL, cognitive function, cost of therapy.

primary.poolable_reason: The four trials surfaced by the strategy question register FOUR DIFFERENT primary composites, differing at the component level: CASTLE-AF and RAFT-AF count all-cause death plus heart-failure events; CABANA counts total mortality, disabling stroke, serious bleeding and cardiac arrest; EAST-AFNET 4 counts CARDIOVASCULAR death, stroke and hospitalisation. One counts all-cause death, another counts cardiovascular death, and two count event classes the others do not. The withholding question was asked at every registered rank and found no shared estimand, because RAFT-AF registers no secondary outcome at all.

single_study_ref.what_this_is: ONE TRIAL'S RESULT, REPORTED AS ONE TRIAL'S RESULT. k = 1. It is the strategy trial proper -- early rhythm control against usual care -- and it is not a pooled estimate and is not presented as one.

the_coherent_pool_is_published_ELSEWHERE.which: CASTLE-AF + RAFT-AF, whose component sets match exactly
the_coherent_pool_is_published_ELSEWHERE.why_not_here: Pooling them again under this topic would put a SECOND COPY of one estimate into the corpus. That is the double-counting P22 measured across the corpus -- 319 summed against 259 distinct identities, 60 double-counted. The sharing is recorded and the pool is referred to rather than repeated.
the_coherent_pool_is_published_ELSEWHERE.why_this_is_a_decision_not_tidiness: Publishing that estimate twice would put a SECOND COPY of one result into a corpus that already double-counts 60 trial identities when its topics are summed -- 319 summed against 259 distinct, measured under P22. Declining to repeat it is therefore a SUBSTANTIVE DECISION about the corpus's arithmetic, not housekeeping, and this page points elsewhere rather than staying silent so that a reader can follow the estimate to its one home.

screening.search_note: mechanical first pass over declared registry fields with enumerated term sets; anything the rules cannot settle is NEEDS_ADJUDICATION
screening.eligibility: ELIGIBILITY turns on whether the trial randomised a RHYTHM-CONTROL STRATEGY against usual care or rate control. A trial in which every arm receives rhythm control -- one drug against another, or ablation against a drug -- does not contrast the strategy and is EXCLUDED on the comparator axis, which is where 125 of the 147 exclusions fall.

risk_of_bias.default_rule: A domain that cannot be judged from the registration and the published report is NO_INFORMATION, never LOW. Low-by-default asserts a fact; high-by-default invents a defect.

ceiling.statement: NO RESULT IN THIS REVIEW CAN REACH LOW RISK OF BIAS ON THE EVIDENCE WE CAN REACH, AND THAT IS A FACT ABOUT OUR ACCESS RATHER THAN ABOUT THE TRIALS. The two domains that would distinguish LOW from SOME CONCERNS need documents this review does not hold: D1 needs allocation concealment and baseline data, which are in neither the registration nor the published abstract; D5 needs the trial's statistical analysis plan, which is not held for any trial. SOME CONCERNS IS THEREFORE THE CEILING, NOT A FINDING. A trial rated SOME CONCERNS here may well be at low risk of bias -- we cannot show it, and we do not imply the opposite.
ceiling.what_would_change_it: Retrieving each trial's full published report and its statistical analysis plan or protocol. Until then the rating is bounded by what we read, and the bound is reported rather than the reader inferring it.
ceiling.why_this_is_stated_rather_than_left_impl: A rating of SOME CONCERNS with no explanation reads as a judgement against the trial. Omitting the reason would manufacture a criticism exactly as a low-by-default manufactures a reassurance -- the same defect pointed the other way.

evidence: `design` states the trial was randomised: 'randomised, open-label; early standardised RHYTHM CONTROL -- antiarrhythmic drugs or ablat'
Allocation concealment and baseline-imbalance data are in neither the registration nor the fields this object holds.

protocol.why: A protocol specified before data collection is a HISTORICAL FACT ABOUT THE PAST and cannot be created retrospectively. Writing one now and calling it prespecified would invalidate every other refusal on these pages, because a reader who caught it would be right to disbelieve all of them.

protocol.authority_permitting_it: MECIR R107 permits post-hoc eligibility criteria PROVIDED THEY ARE DECLARED AS SUCH. They are declared, here and on the page, and the page says 'derived, post hoc' in its heading.
protocol.forward_remedy: For topics not yet built, a protocol is to be written and registered BEFORE the search is executed, so that the claim becomes true GOING FORWARD. It is never to be made true retroactively for a built topic.

manuscript.introduction:
This review asks: In adults with atrial fibrillation, does an early rhythm-control STRATEGY -- antiarrhythmic drugs or ablation, chosen and escalated as a strategy rather than as a single procedure -- reduce cardiovascular death, stroke or hospitalisation compared with usual care?

It examines 1 randomised trial and DOES NOT POOL THEM, against usual care.

The outcome sought is Each trial's own registered primary composite.

Everything in this paragraph is derived from stored fields and none of it is authored. The interpretive sentences that follow are marked as drafts and are the author's to replace.

bookkeeping_2026_08_21._what: The five reporting claims a PRISMA-2020 manuscript needs that are FETCHABLE rather than argued -- each derived from a field here, or stated as an honest absence.
bookkeeping_2026_08_21.which_limbs_this_review_refuses: Of the four properties this project requires of a completed topic, 1 are held (rob per result) and 3 are refused with the obstacle named in the evidence (comparison denominator, grade per pool, model output verbatim).
bookkeeping_2026_08_21.the_search_its_date_and_its_databases: PRIMARY TRIALS. NO BIBLIOGRAPHIC SEARCH FOR PRIMARY TRIALS WAS RUN. The 1 included trial was identified by reading named registration on the dates recorded on each entry.
bookkeeping_2026_08_21.whether_this_review_was_prospectively_re: NO PROSPERO REGISTRATION OR PROTOCOL RECORD IS HELD ON THIS OBJECT. That is not the same as knowing this review was not registered, and neither claim is made. It is recorded here as an absence so that a reader does not have to infer it from silence.
bookkeeping_2026_08_21.that_two_assessors_disagreed_and_where: Risk of bias was assessed independently a second time by GPT-5 Codex (openai family), via `codex exec`, blind to this assessment and given the same registry facts. 4 of 6 judgements -- 66.7%. Reported as DISAGREEMENT: agreement between two assessors given the same facts authenticates nothing. By domain: D1 1 of 1 disagree, D2 0 of 1 disagree, D3 1 of 1 disagree, D4 0 of 1 disagree, D5 1 of 1 disagree, OVERALL 1 of 1 disagree.
bookkeeping_2026_08_21.which_risk_of_bias_domains_drove_the_rat: Where a result is rated worse than LOW overall, the domain carrying that judgement is: D2 on 1 result(s), D5 on 1 result(s). The overall rating is the worst domain, so these are the domains that determine it.
